hypotheses.setup_conditions: High ADR stocks, high volume/liquidity, daily chart trend-following breakout, sector momentum
hypotheses.statistical_claim: Overnight and swing trades generally outperformed intraday same-day longs in verified P&L analysis
hypotheses.invalidation_risk: Fails if sector momentum reverses or stock lacks overnight follow-through liquidity

hypotheses.holding_period: Strictly same-day intraday (close before market close)

hypotheses.invalidation_risk: Holding short positions overnight exposes trades to catastrophic gap-ups and adverse drift

hypotheses.title: Minimum 4% ADR (Average Daily Range) Volatility Filter
hypotheses.hypothesis_statement: Sustainable trading edge requires sufficient price range expansion; traders should filter for stocks exhibiting ADR > 4% with strong liquidity. Equities with ADR < 3-4% lack the range necessary to compensate for trade execution costs and risk.
hypotheses.setup_conditions: ADR >= 4.0%, high daily volume, high liquidity (e.g. semiconductors, memory, storage)
hypotheses.statistical_claim: Strongest historical trading results concentrated exclusively in high ADR stocks; flat/negative on low ADR
hypotheses.invalidation_risk: Trading stocks with ADR < 3% leads to breakeven or losing performance due to range compression

hypotheses.title: Exponential Bet Sizing on High-Conviction A+ Setups
hypotheses.hypothesis_statement: Uniform position sizing across all trades destroys profitability by treating high-probability and low-probability setups equally; capital allocation must be exponentially skewed toward A+ setups that meet all focus criteria, while sizing down drastically or abstaining from marginal setups.
hypotheses.setup_conditions: Confirmed A+ setup matching full focus filter checklist (rare occurrence, non-daily)
hypotheses.statistical_claim: Allocating equal size to best and worst trades was the primary leak in trading performance
hypotheses.invalidation_risk: Over-sizing on non-A+ setups leads to drawdowns; if every trade looks like A+, grading is flawed
hypotheses.verbatim_quote: warrants more size, less size, or no trade at all. There's a really fancy term called exponential bet sizing. It really just means to size into your best A+ setups when they appear and trade in much smaller on the average setups and everything else. Naturally, that also means the best of the best setups for you should not appear every single day. If every trade looks like an A+ setup, then you probably need to fix your grading systems or your analysis. Remember, you don't have to trade every day, every week, or even every month.
